record.paper_title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems
record.original_question: Can a bifurcation theory for quaternion-valued differential equations be developed for systems subjected to perturbations, and in particular how should an appropriate Poincare map be defined in the quaternion-valued setting so that bifurcation phenomena can be studied rigorously?

evidence.quote: For QDEs, I guess that the bifurcations can occur if it is subjected to some perturbations. The difficulty is how to define the Poincar´e map? This is challenging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of quaternions, with elements $q = q_0 + q_1 i + q_2 j + q_3 k$ where $i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1$. Consider quaternion-valued differential equations (QDEs) of the form
$$\dot{x}(t) = F(x(t), \mu), \qquad x(t) \in \mathbb{H}^n,\ \mu \in \mathbb{R}^p,$$
where $F : \mathbb{H}^n \times \mathbb{R}^p \to \mathbb{H}^n$ depends smoothly on a parameter $\mu$ and may be viewed as a perturbation of an unperturbed system $\dot{x} = F_0(x)$.

Develop a rigorous bifurcation theory for such QDEs under parameter perturbations. In particular:

(a) Provide an intrinsic definition of a Poincaré (first-return) map for QDEs that respects the non-commutative quaternionic structure—specifying what plays the role of a transverse cross-section to a periodic orbit in $\mathbb{H}^n$, in what sense the map is well-defined and smooth, and how it relates to (but is not merely a real $4n$-dimensional reduction of) the underlying flow.

(b) Using this Poincaré map, formulate and prove analogues of classical bifurcation results (e.g., saddle-node, period-doubling, Hopf/Neimark–Sacker bifurcations of periodic orbits) for QDEs subjected to perturbations, identifying the genuinely quaternionic phenomena that arise and conditions under which bifurcations occur.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication appears to provide an intrinsic definition of a Poincaré map for quaternion-valued ODEs or a corresponding bifurcation theory. Existing work on bifurcations in quaternion-valued systems (e.g., Hopf bifurcation for fractional-order quaternion-valued neural networks) proceeds by decomposing the QDE into an equivalent real-valued system rather than working intrinsically over $\mathbb{H}$, leaving the posed problem open.

status_evidence.title: New exploration on bifurcation for fractional-order quaternion-valued neural networks involving leakage delays
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers decompose the fractional-order quaternion-valued delayed neural networks into equivalent real-valued networks using the Hamilton rule of quaternion algebra, then derive bifurcation conditions using stability criteria of fractional-order differential dynamical systems.
status_evidence.claim: Bifurcation results for quaternion-valued systems in the literature are obtained via real-valued reductions, not via an intrinsic quaternionic Poincaré map.
